title: Why Did the Titanic Sink So Fast?
description:
The Titanic was the largest moving object ever built by humans. It had sixteen watertight compartments, electric doors that closed with one switch on the bridge, and a reputation for being practically unsinkable. It hit an iceberg at eleven forty at night, and two hours and forty minutes later, it was gone. The hole was not even big. Today, ten parts of the Titanic, and how each one helped a giant ship sink so fast.

Machine Reverse takes apart the machines you see every day and explains, part by part, why each one exists. This video covers 10 parts.

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:29 1. The walls that stopped too low
2:59 2. The double bottom
4:29 3. The rivets
6:08 4. The cold steel
7:36 5. The rudder
9:13 6. The center propeller
10:47 7. The crow's nest
12:11 8. The wireless room
13:46 9. The lifeboats
15:20 10. The expansion joint
16:50 The verdict

Sources:
- Bulkheads, compartments, damage and timeline: British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry report (1912) https://www.titanicinquiry.org/BOTInq/BOTReport/botRep01.php
- US Senate Inquiry into the Titanic disaster (1912), testimony of Frederick Fleet, Harold Bride and others https://www.titanicinquiry.org/USInq/USReport/AmInq01.php
- Ship particulars, double bottom, propulsion and rudder: Wikipedia, "Titanic" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Titanic
- Olympic refit after Titanic (inner skin, raised bulkheads): Wikipedia, "RMS Olympic" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RMS_Olympic
- Wrought iron rivets with slag: J. Hooper McCarty and T. Foecke, "What Really Sank the Titanic" (2008); NIST summary https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2008/04/nist-metallurgist-finds-clues-titanic-sinking
- Brittle steel at -2 C: K. Felkins, H. Leighly, A. Jankovic, "The Royal Mail Ship Titanic: Did a Metallurgical Failure Cause a Night to Remember?", JOM 50 (1998) https://www.tms.org/pubs/journals/jom/9801/felkins-9801.html
- Binocular locker key sold at auction (2007): BBC News https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/7017785.stm
- Lifeboat regulations and capacity: Wikipedia, "Lifeboats of the Titanic" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifeboats_of_the_Titanic
- SOLAS 1914 and the International Ice Patrol: IMO, "International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), 1974" (history) https://www.imo.org/en/About/Conventions/Pages/International-Convention-for-the-Safety-of-Life-at-Sea-(SOLAS),-1974.aspx
- SS Californian and the radio messages: Wikipedia, "SS Californian" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Californian
- Wreck discovery (1985, depth, bow and stern separation): Wikipedia, "Wreck of the Titanic" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wreck_of_the_Titanic
